title: The Wonder Nobody Can Find
description: Did the Hanging Gardens of Babylon really exist?

scenes.narration: One of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World may never have existed.
scenes.image_prompt: lush terraced gardens with waterfalls rising above an ancient Mesopotamian city

scenes.narration: Ancient writers describe gardens rising in terraces above Babylon, in today's Iraq.
scenes.image_prompt: ancient Babylon with ziggurat, blue Ishtar gate and the Euphrates river

scenes.narration: Legend says King Nebuchadnezzar the Second built them for his homesick wife.
scenes.image_prompt: Babylonian king and queen on a palace terrace looking at green gardens

scenes.narration: Trees and flowers grow on stone terraces, watered by machines lifting water from the river.
scenes.image_prompt: ancient water-lifting machine with wheels and buckets raising water to terraces

scenes.narration: But Babylonian records from his reign never mention them.
scenes.image_prompt: clay cuneiform tablets on a table in an ancient archive, lamp light

scenes.narration: Archaeologists have dug at Babylon for over a century without clear proof.
scenes.image_prompt: archaeologists excavating mud-brick ruins in the Iraqi desert, early 20th century

scenes.narration: One scholar argues they were actually in Nineveh, built by a different king.
scenes.image_prompt: ancient Assyrian city of Nineveh with palace gardens and an aqueduct

scenes.narration: Real, myth, or in the wrong city? What do you think?
scenes.image_prompt: ruins of ancient Babylon at sunset, desert haze
